findings.title: Holdout measurement session launches with full-env inheritance, auto-approve permissions and no OS sandbox
findings.problem: `LAUNCH_ARGV` launches the measured `claude` session with `--permission-mode dontAsk` (line 90), so Bash/Write/Edit tool calls execute without any permission prompt. `session_environment()` (docs/design/holdout-v2.12/tools/holdout_eval_launch.py ~line 185-191) builds the session's environment as `os.environ` minus only `STRIPPED_ENV` — a 6-item Anthropic-auth-specific denylist defined in holdout_autopilot.py:110-112 (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`, `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`). Any other secret the owner's Terminal environment carries (GitHub tokens, cloud credentials, SSH agent vars, unrelated API keys) is passed through unfiltered. The settings file used for this launch (`docs/design/b3-ground-truth/b3-runner-v2.12/settings-measured.json`) carries no `sandbox`/network-blocking key at all (contrast with the fix-harness's explicit `network: {allowedDomains: [], strictAllowlist: true}` Seatbelt policy). The session reviews holdout case content that is, by the kit's own design, security/vulnerability-themed material.
findings.fix_hint: switch session_environment() to an explicit allowlist of the env keys the session actually needs (mirroring freeze_manifest.ENV_ALLOWLIST) rather than a denylist of Anthropic-auth keys only, and add an explicit sandbox/network-block policy (as harness_sandbox.build_session_settings does) to the runner settings template used for this launch.
findings.why_it_matters: If the reviewed content manages to prompt-inject the model into running a Bash command (no permission gate blocks this under `dontAsk`), any non-Anthropic secret present in the owner's environment can be read and, absent a network sandbox, exfiltrated — a class of attack indirect prompt injection against LLM review agents is known to enable.

findings.title: B3 measured review session pre-authorizes Bash/Write/Edit via --allowedTools with inherited shell environment and no OS sandbox
findings.problem: The `session` block execs `claude --permission-mode manual ... --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Write,Edit,Grep,Glob,Task,Agent"`. `--allowedTools` pre-authorizes those tools, so despite `--permission-mode manual`, Bash/Write/Edit calls do not raise a permission card for `run_case.sh`'s die()-on-unexpected-card logic to catch. The `launch` block starts this process with `env "REPO=$REPO" ... bash -c "$SESSION_SHELL" ...` (common.sh, `launch` block) — `env` without `-i` adds those vars on top of, rather than replacing, whatever environment the tmux-server-launching shell already had, which the runbook itself documents at length ("a tmux pane inherits the environment of whichever shell started the tmux server"). Unlike the fix-harness (harness_sandbox.build_session_settings, which sets `network: {allowedDomains: [], strictAllowlist: true}` and a custom per-call `can_use_tool` gate), no OS-level sandbox or outbound-network restriction is configured anywhere in settings-measured.json or this runbook for the B3 session.
findings.fix_hint: give the B3 measured session the same kind of OS-level sandbox/network-block policy the fix-harness uses, and/or scope its environment to an explicit allowlist instead of inheriting the launching shell's environment plus overrides.
findings.why_it_matters: A B3 case that successfully prompt-injects the reviewing model gets unprompted Bash execution in an environment that includes whatever the owner's shell/tmux server environment holds, with no sandbox blocking outbound network — a realistic path to secret exfiltration from the operator's own machine.

findings.title: settings_is_fail_closed() never verifies the sandbox network policy
findings.problem: `settings_is_fail_closed()` is the single authoritative check `drive()` uses to decide a session's settings are actually locked down (mutation-tested extensively elsewhere in this diff). It checks `disableClaudeAiConnectors`, the new env pins, `sandbox.enabled/failIfUnavailable/allowUnsandboxedCommands/excludedCommands`, and every filesystem deny/allow rule — but never inspects `sandbox.network` (`allowedDomains`/`strictAllowlist`), which is what actually blocks the sandboxed session's network egress. This gap predates this diff (the `network` key in `build_session_settings` is unchanged context, not touched by this PR's lines) and is not demonstrated to be reachable today, since only `build_session_settings()` ever constructs this dict.
findings.current_code:
def settings_is_fail_closed(settings):
    """True only when every containment lock is present in `settings`."""
    try:
        sb = settings["sandbox"]
        ...
        return bool(
            settings.get("disableClaudeAiConnectors") is True
            and isinstance(env, dict)
            and all(env.get(k) == v for k, v in SESSION_ENV_PINS.items())
            and sb.get("enabled") is True
            ... )
findings.fix_hint: add network-policy fields (sb["network"]["allowedDomains"] == [] and sb["network"]["strictAllowlist"] is True) to the settings_is_fail_closed() assertion, mirroring how every other lock is checked and mutation-tested.
findings.why_it_matters: If a future change ever builds session settings from a different code path (or a mutation silently drops the network block), settings_is_fail_closed() would still report the settings as fail-closed and drive() would launch — defeating the one network-egress control that currently mitigates full-environment inheritance into the sandboxed session (see harness_driver_sdk.session_env). pending: a change that drops or alters sandbox.network while keeping every other field would demonstrate this.

findings.title: Fix-harness sandboxed session inherits the full parent process environment
findings.problem: `session_env()` copies `os.environ` wholesale into the Agent SDK session's env, only removing `CLAUDECODE` and forcing `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false`. Any secret in the orchestrator's own environment (API keys, tokens) is handed to the sandboxed fix-agent session. This is mitigated by `build_session_settings()`'s explicit `network: {allowedDomains: [], strictAllowlist: true}` Seatbelt policy, which blocks outbound network for Bash and everything it spawns, and this function is unchanged by the current diff (only the `model=` parameter was added here).
findings.current_code:
def session_env(environ=None, tmp_root=None):
    env = dict(os.environ if environ is None else environ)
    env.pop("CLAUDECODE", None)
    env["ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS"] = "false"
    ...
    return env
findings.fix_hint: project the session's env through an explicit allowlist (as freeze_manifest.ENV_ALLOWLIST does) instead of forwarding the full parent environment, as defense in depth alongside the network block.
findings.why_it_matters: If the network-blocking sandbox policy is ever weakened or bypassed (see sec-003), the full-environment inheritance here would become a direct path to secret exposure for a prompt-injected session; today it is mitigated. pending: a path that lets a sandboxed Bash call reach the network despite allowedDomains: [] would demonstrate this.

findings.title: Secret-shaped-value scan is a narrow denylist, not an allowlist
findings.problem: `SECRET_VALUE_RE` only matches a fixed set of known credential shapes (`sk-ant-`, `Bearer `, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `xox[abp]-`, `AKIA...`, PEM private-key headers). A credential in another shape (a generic password, a Slack legacy token, a cloud key not matching these prefixes) would not trip `_scan_values`. This is substantially mitigated by `MANIFEST_SCHEMA` being a closed, per-field-regex allowlist (CRED_FIELD_RE refuses credential-named fields outright; most free-form-looking fields are actually restricted to hex/version/model-id shapes), so the scan is a secondary, defense-in-depth layer rather than the primary control, and I did not find a specific manifest field whose allowed shape is loose enough to carry an unmatched secret end-to-end.
findings.fix_hint: broaden SECRET_VALUE_RE with a few more common shapes (AWS secret keys, generic bearer/JWT patterns, GitHub fine-grained PATs `github_pat_`) as additional defense in depth, even though the schema allowlist is the primary control.
findings.why_it_matters: A secret that matches none of the pinned patterns and happens to land in a schema field whose shape regex is permissive enough would be committed into the manifest undetected. pending: name a MANIFEST_SCHEMA field whose regex is loose enough to carry an unmatched secret shape.

findings.title: Identity check silently passes the .vibe-check.toml check when clone_dir is omitted for holdout-eval
findings.problem: `_check_toml_absent` returns `[]` (pass, no problem) when `live["clone_dir"]` is None and the runner is `holdout-eval`, deferring the check to whichever caller supplies a clone dir. Every production caller I found does pass `clone_dir` for this runner (holdout_eval_launch.py's `verify(... clone_dir=run_dir ...)`), so this fail-open path appears unreachable in practice today; it is reachable only by a direct, non-production call to `freeze_check.verify(runner='holdout-eval')` that omits `clone_dir`.
findings.fix_hint: make the holdout-eval branch fail closed too (return a problem) rather than silently passing, matching the b3 branch, so a future caller that forgets clone_dir cannot get a false IDENTITY OK.
findings.why_it_matters: If a future holdout-eval caller is added (or an existing one refactored) without clone_dir, this branch would let a top_model-source mismatch (e.g. an unintended .vibe-check.toml override) through undetected. pending: a production caller that omits clone_dir for holdout-eval would demonstrate this is live, not dead code.

agent_notes: The freeze-kit (freeze_check.py, freeze_common.py, freeze_manifest.py, freeze_policy.py, freeze_tally.py, semgrep_replica.py) and the fix-harness's commit-based plugin materialization are unusually well defended: strict rev/path validation (no shell metacharacters, no '..', no absolute paths), O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW on every write, explicit symlink refusal when materializing a plugin tree from git objects, no subprocess shell=True anywhere, and extensive mutation-tested locks for every security-relevant invariant (no-override, fail-closed, no-worktree-copy, etc.). I did not find an exploitable injection, path-traversal or deserialization defect in this area.

review_archive.py (plugin) is a clean no-clobber archive implementation: os.link (fails on existing target) + os.unlink, phase names restricted to a fixed charset with an 'unknown' fallback, retry loop bounded at 1000 attempts. No path-traversal or TOCTOU issue found.

holdout_eval_launch.py and holdout_autopilot.py correctly never read, list or hash anything under the sealed case folder — confirmed both by code inspection (slot_identity only touches os.path.basename) and by a test that makes the case folder mode 000 and still launches successfully. The retune seal-order proof in freeze_policy.py is likewise checked purely by git commit topology and file names, never by reading SEAL.json content.

score.py's new needs_verification placeholder-normalization logic (_NV_PLACEHOLDERS) is a scoring/quality change, not a security control; I did not evaluate it for security impact beyond confirming it introduces no new injection or deserialization surface.
